thread:
nina: Heads-up: after yesterday's pre-accept optimization we see rare SSE resume corruption + duplicate events for a subset of routes. Low rate (~1%), but reproducible.

omar: Any logs?

nina: snippet:
```
[2026-05-01T14:03:21Z] client=cid-77 resume=rt_77 proxy=px-eu accept
[2026-05-01T14:03:21Z] route_pick: fallback->pool-2 due to hotness
[2026-05-01T14:03:21Z] backend=shard-2 replay_expected=240 replay_seen=3 -> seq_mismatch
[2026-05-01T14:03:21Z] emit duplicate_event id=ev_4411
```

tess: Pre-accept makes sense for latency, but looks like we accept before final pool mapping, so token intended for pool-1 can be accepted then routed to pool-2.

kai: Proposed short fix: validate token.pool_ns against chosen pool before finalizing accept. If mismatch, reject and force full reconnect. Metric: resume.pool_mismatch_count{region,pool}.

omar: Agreed. Also add trace tags token.pool_ns and chosen.pool for easier triage.

tess: Console UX: add a small "deduped resumes" stat and a filter for pool_mismatch=true in per-route billing. Customers seeing double charges.

nina: Rollout plan: feature-flag the new validation; canary 2% eu then 10%. Emit resume.reject:pool_mismatch trace and metric.

kai: Long-term: include pool_ns and route_version in token signature so acceptance is deterministic. Also consider moving routing before accept if validation adds too much complexity.

ops-bot: canary playbook -> https://deploy.internal/redwood/playbooks/1722223333

omar: I'll implement the validation + metric today. Tess/Kai can wire traces and console patch.

tess: I'll add the console filter and backfill script to mark deduped events for last 72h.

nina: Thanks. Keep this thread for any odd event ids we find during canary.
